key_insight: The paper reframes on-policy distillation as a reinforcement-learning problem and introduces LSPD, a distillation method that improves sample efficiency by combining optimistic exploration with reuse of past rollouts.
engineering_relevance: For LLM reasoning systems, LSPD offers a practical way to reduce rollout cost while preserving diversity and maintaining or improving benchmark performance.
method: Connects OPD's reverse-KL objective to KL-regularized policy optimization.
Introduces least-square policy distillation with optimistic exploration inspired by value-based RL.
Reuses previously collected trajectories in an off-policy manner to improve rollout efficiency.
evidence_signal: Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks and multiple teacher-student settings, LSPD improves Avg@16 by +1.59 points on average, and its fully off-policy variant matches vanilla OPD using only the first 25% of rollout batches.
watch_item: The strongest efficiency gains rely on an idealized formulation and careful off-policy reuse, so practical stability and exploration design may be sensitive to implementation details.
paper_title: An RL View of OPD: Least Square Policy Distillation for Sample-Efficient LLM Reasoning
